title: Quick check: Cross-Origin Resource Sharing

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Cross-Origin Resource Sharing”?
options: The browser will infer all application behavior even if inputs and state are contradictory.
The concept allows application code to mutate React-managed DOM and state directly.
Understanding CORS must respect trust boundaries; authorization and secrets are not protected by client-side UI alone.
The concept removes the need to consider error states or accessibility.
questions.answer_key: Understanding CORS must respect trust boundaries; authorization and secrets are not protected by client-side UI alone.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Cross-Origin Resource Sharing: Understanding CORS must respect trust boundaries; authorization and secrets are not protected by client-side UI alone.

questions.prompt: Which practice is most reliable when applying Understanding CORS?
options: Optimize by adding every available Hook without measuring the result.
Keep secret keys and authorization checks on a trusted server.
Skip validation because a successful render proves that the application is correct.
Store duplicate copies of every value so each component can change it independently.
questions.answer_key: Keep secret keys and authorization checks on a trusted server.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Cross-Origin Resource Sharing: Keep secret keys and authorization checks on a trusted server.

questions.prompt: What should you verify before considering “Cross-Origin Resource Sharing” complete?
options: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
Check only whether the file exists; syntax and runtime behavior do not matter.
Assume a client-side check proves that a remote service accepted the change.
Rely only on a screenshot of the happy path and never repeat the test.
questions.answer_key: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Cross-Origin Resource Sharing: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
